answer: A river delta gives each agent one staff gauge where a karst spring feeds one channel. Each week the agent releases a tracer dye plume upstream and logs the minute it reaches the gauge, and a downstream checker re-times every tenth release and voids any log whose plume arrives too fast or too slow for that channel length. A second gauge under one name voids both claims for a season. To run a thousand fake gauges, an attacker must tend a thousand channels, release a thousand timed dye plumes, and pass a thousand re-timings against real water flow.
